summary.headline: AAVAS Q4FY26: net profit up 18% YoY to Rs 1.82 bn, NIM up 44 bps QoQ to 8.45%, GNPA 1.05%; management targets 20%+ AUM growth aspiration.
summary.overview: Q4FY26 disbursements rose 16% YoY and 36% QoQ to Rs 23.5 bn, and net profit grew 18% YoY to Rs 1.82 bn on 17% NII growth. FY26 AUM reached Rs 234.5 bn (up 15% YoY) while FY26 disbursements grew 11% to Rs 67.8 bn, below the aspiration. Asset quality improved sequentially, with 1+ DPD at 3.17% (down 63 bps QoQ) and GNPA at 1.05% (down 14 bps QoQ). Management acknowledged weak volume productivity and opex growth outpacing AUM, and is pushing risk-adjusted pricing and direct sourcing to address these.

financial_highlights.metric: Net interest margin (Q4FY26, on total assets)

financial_highlights.change: +38 bps QoQ; net worth growth 16% YoY

segments.name: Home loans / core retail (assessed income)
segments.commentary: Management cites best-in-class underwriting in the assessed income segment; Q4 home loan volumes declined YoY per analyst analysis, with the company acknowledging volume productivity as an immediate focus area. Borrower repayment rates rose mainly due to prepayments, with balance transfer-outs held at 5.5% for FY26 against a sub-6% cap.

segments.name: Geographies
segments.commentary: Vintage states show 1+ DPD and GNPA well below 4% and 1.25% of AUM; emerging markets are at 1+ DPD within 4% and GNPA within 1% of AUM. Q4 branch additions were concentrated in Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat, with focus also on Maharashtra and southern states.

guidance_outlook: Long-term aspiration of consistent 20%+ AUM growth, outperforming the industry; no specific FY27 growth number given.
ROE target set in the high teens (current Q4FY26 ROE 14.67%).
Spreads to be maintained at 5%+ despite PLR cuts, with the slight yield placement improvement expected to offset cost of borrowing stabilising.
Opex-to-AUM targeted below 3% on a 2-3 year horizon; the CFO's earlier comment indicates 2.75% once the balance sheet doubles.
Credit cost guidance maintained below 25 bps on a sustainable basis; no move into riskier segments.
Management expects branch investments to yield results in the next full year, with growth expected to recover in FY27.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded to 435 across 15 states after 31 additions in Q4FY26, with focus on Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra and southern states.
Technology: most capitalisation done on Oracle FLEXCUBE and Oracle Fusion ERP; only small annual spend planned for collection software and AI/GenAI in underwriting and collections.
Opex rose YoY in FY26 due to branch-expansion manpower, new ESOP/PSOP retention scheme after CVC entry, and lower-than-planned growth in denominators.
Management expects the branch and people investments to start producing results in the next full year.
demand_pricing: Competition intensified in Q4 as lenders pushed to underwrite volume in the year-end quarter; management says it does not see competition materially affecting yield placement over the full year.
Yield decline of about 20 bps QoQ in Q4 was attributed mainly to a 15 bps PLR cut effective 1 March 2026; a further 10 bps PLR cut is expected in June per an analyst.
Management is shifting toward risk-adjusted pricing at branch level; it says early results are visible but the journey is gradual.
Average ticket size is to move only with inflation; no deliberate ticket-size expansion.
April 2026 bounce rates were lower than March and lower than April 2025, per the CRO; the Middle East war has not yet shown up in collections.
Sourcing mix: management is rebuilding direct sourcing (branch-driven, CSC, website, app with referral programme) while stating indirect channels will continue.

qa_highlights.question: Where does the sector's medium-term growth stand and what are FY27/FY28 growth targets, and where does ROE settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Aspiration is 20%+ AUM growth. Near-term focus is sharper execution across product, channel mix, geography and funnel leakages. High-teens ROE is the long-term target.

qa_highlights.question: With the PLR cut, how will spreads and disbursement yields evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a full-year cost of borrowing reduction of 62 bps stabilising, spread at 5.2%, and confidence in maintaining spreads at 5%+ via better product placement. It did not give a quantified yield outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth been below 20% for two years and what is the channel plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed past performance to different variables and times. It plans to rebuild direct sourcing muscle while keeping indirect channels, and to invest in southern and other high-potential states.

qa_highlights.question: Has risk-adjusted pricing started and does higher yield imply higher risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing improvement began in FY26 across 435 branches and is progressing gradually. Management said higher yield does not mean higher risk and that it will not enter riskier segments or breach credit cost guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is competition from larger HFCs entering the company's ticket sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 competition was a seasonal year-end push. It does not see a structural competitive impact on yields over the full year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the opex-to-AUM trajectory and what are the tech-led efficiency use cases?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex rose in FY26 for branch and ESOP reasons. Management targets below 3% over 2-3 years and expects the branch investment to pay off in FY27. Tech spend is limited to small collection-software and AI investments.

qa_highlights.question: Why have loan volumes been flat or down despite headcount and branch growth, and what changed in April?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called this an immediate priority, reported improved April numbers, and said productivity per person and revenue per field employee will be tracked quarterly. It also noted a shift to requiring realised instrument receipt in customer accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did repayment rates rise while balance transfer-outs fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance transfer-outs were 5.5% for FY26 against a sub-6% cap. The rise in repayments was mainly from customer prepayments and part-payments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to the Middle East war and inflation shock?
qa_highlights.answer: No adverse trend in bounces or collections so far. The company is not financing energy-linked or directly affected profiles and is tracking 5-6 profiles it considers at risk.

risks_watch: Volume productivity: FY26 disbursement count was flat and home loan volumes were down YoY per analyst analysis, despite a larger headcount and branch base.
Yield pressure from PLR cuts, with a further 10 bps cut expected in June, and a possible ROA moderation in H1FY27 as flagged by an analyst.
Opex-to-AUM rose in FY26; delivery of the sub-3% target depends on FY27 growth recovery.
Risk-adjusted pricing push could raise credit risk; management reiterated the sub-25 bps credit cost guidance.
Macro exposure to the Middle East war, fuel price inflation and Tier 2/3 borrower stress; watch April-June bounce and 1+ DPD trends.
Competitive intensity from larger HFCs in affordable housing, particularly in quarter-end pushes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, funding costs and the 20%+ growth ambition, but notably defensive on the FY26 volume shortfall, the sub-par growth record, and yield improvement, which it framed as a gradual, in-progress journey without quantified targets. Management used hindsight framing and repeated its credit-first stance when pressed on pricing.
key_quotes: Our aspiration clearly is to consistently deliver 20% -plus AUM growth, largely to outperform industry.
increase in yield by no manner suggests increase of risk. I will repeat that, increase of yield by no standards equals mathematically to increase of risk.
This is a year of landmarks and milestones.
It is very clear to us that this is an area of immediate attention for all of us .
We are shooting for something below 3%. However, as I mentioned, it's a journey.

adds.what: 31 new branches added in Q4FY26 (435 branches across 15 states)

growth.why: Management aspires to consistent 20%+ AUM growth but gave no FY27 number; growth is expected to recover in FY27 from branch and people investments, with Q4 disbursements up 16% YoY and 36% QoQ, while FY26 disbursements grew only 11% and home loan volumes fell YoY.
